name: Mercury
headline: diameter
subtitle: Innermost planet of the Solar System
description: Mercury is the smallest planet in the Solar System and the closest to the Sun, orbiting at an average of about 57.9 million km. NASA's Planetary Fact Sheet gives it an equatorial diameter of 4,879 km, a little over a third of Earth's, and a mass of about 3.3 × 10²³ kg. It has no moons and almost no atmosphere.

facts.text: Mercury's mass is 0.0553 times Earth's and its volume 0.0562 times Earth's.
Mercury takes 87.969 days to orbit the Sun, and one solar day (sunrise to sunrise) lasts 4,222.6 hours.
Mercury has no natural satellites, and its surface pressure is less than about 5 × 10⁻¹⁵ bar.
Mercury's mean density is 5,429 kg/m³, close to Earth's 5,513 kg/m³.

caveats: The headline diameter (4,879 km) comes from the summary Planetary Fact Sheet; twice the equatorial radius on the Mercury Fact Sheet gives 4,881 km.
Mercury is very nearly a sphere; its polar radius is only about 2 km less than its equatorial radius.
